MANILA, Philippines — Inclement weather did not stop the entrepreneurs of La Union from trooping to SM City La Union yesterday to participate in Go Negosyo’s Trabaho at Negosyo.
Go Negosyo founder Joey Concepcion said more Trabaho and Negosyo events will be rolled out as the Philippines chairs ASEAN this year.
“This will help bring the vision of inclusive prosperity in ASEAN to more Filipinos nationwide,” he said.

In the photo giving the signature Go Negosyo thumbs-up with the job seekers and MSMEs are DTI-La Union acting provincial director Victoria Ordoño, Sangguniang Panlalawigan board members Eulogio Clarence Martin de Guzman III, Miguel Corleone Magsaysay and Kristine Sibuma; Plato Wraps CEO Kamela Seen; Sangguniang Panlalawigan board member Maria Rosario Eufrosina Nisce; La Union provincial administrator Ramon Torres; La Union Gov. Mario Eduardo Ortega; But First, Coffee founder and CEO Anna Isabelle Magalona-Go; La Union Chamber of Commerce and Industry president Anne Maureen Tan and SM City La Union mall manager Drake Lim.

Trabaho at Negosyo is Go Negosyo’s nationwide free entrepreneurship mentoring and job fair event held in urban areas across the Philippines. The next stop for Trabaho at Negosyo is the city of Iligan in Northern Mindanao on Oct. 24.

articles.title: Robinsons Land, MMDA enhance mobility across key Metro Manila routes
articles.summary: Robinsons Land Corp. has strengthened its support for urban mobility through its partnership with the MMDA Love Bus program, deploying two dedicated RLC buses that will serve key commuter corridors,…

blocks.text: September 13, 2026 | 12:00am

Robinsons Land has helped advance the MMDA Love Bus program with the deployment of two RLC buses to serve key commuter corridors connecting Quezon City and Pasig City. Photo shows Victor Nuñez, MMDA Traffic Enforcement Group director; Tina Real-Lim, Robinsons Malls deputy general manager; Mybelle Aragon-GoBio, Robinsons Land president and CEO; Romando Artes, MMDA chairman; Faraday Go, Robinsons Land EVP and Group Business Unit general manager; Gerald Tambis, head of Robinsons Destination Estates and Bambie Andal, Robinsons Land VP for public-private partnerships.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — Robinsons Land Corp. (RLC) has strengthened its support for urban mobility through its partnership with the MMDA Love Bus program, deploying two dedicated RLC buses that will serve key commuter corridors, connecting to some of Metro Manila’s busiest districts – Quezon City and Pasig City.

This initiative provides commuters with a more convenient and accessible transport option while helping ease traffic congestion along major routes that traverse Ortigas Business District as well as the growing business communities in Bridgetowne, RLC’s premier destination estate.

“Robinsons Land recognizes the growing need for efficient mobility solutions that will help Filipinos navigate their daily travel challenge,” said Mybelle Aragon GoBio, president and CEO of Robinsons Land.

By extending transportation access across high-traffic areas, the MMDA Love Bus initiative aims to reduce commuting friction, support productivity and make every day journeys more seamless for thousands of Filipino workers, students and residents.

The deployment of RLC buses reflects the company’s commitment to creating developments and partnerships that deliver meaningful benefits beyond its properties and contribute to more connected communities.

The launch was attended by First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, together with Metro Manila mayors, government officials and Robinsons Land executives, led by Aragon-GoBio and EVP and Group Business Unit general manager of Robinsons Malls and Robinsons Destination Estates Faraday Go.

The collaboration highlights the shared commitment of public and private sector stakeholders to advancing practical transportation solutions that improve mobility, ease daily commutes and enhance the overall quality of life for Filipinos.

articles.title: Leptospirosis cases still high
articles.summary: There is still a high admission of leptospirosis cases at the San Lazaro Hospital, with the majority of cases already in the severe stage.

blocks.text: September 13, 2026 | 12:00am
Nurses and Philippine Red Cross medical assistants attend to patients diagnosed with leptospirosis at the emergency room and wards of San Lazaro Hospital in Sta. Cruz, Manila, on August 26, 2026.
Noel Pabalate / The Philippine STAR
MANILA, Philippines — There is still a high admission of leptospirosis cases at the San Lazaro Hospital (SLH), with the majority of cases already in the severe stage.
In a radio interview yesterday, SLH’s Adult Infectious Diseases and Tropical Medicine Department head Dr. Rontgene Solante said their current leptospirosis patient admissions stand at 10 to 15 a day.
He noted that last week, leptospirosis admissions at SLH was 20 to 30 a day.
“We thought at this point our admission rate is already on a decline. But it is not really decreasing,” he said.
Solante explained that if a person waded in floodwater, the earliest appearance of leptospirosis symptoms could be on the third to fifth day. “But it can be as long as two weeks,” he said.
Solante reminded the public that doxycycline prophylaxis should never be taken without a doctor’s prescription, particularly for pregnant women and children below eight years old.
“There are alternative medications, but they need to consult a doctor first,” he said.

To prevent leptospirosis, the SLH reminded the public to avoid wading in floodwaters, wash body parts exposed to floods with soap and clean water, keep surroundings clean and free from rodents, drink clean water, eat well-cooked food and consult a doctor immediately if experiencing symptoms.
Latest data from the Department of Health showed that 6,253 leptospirosis cases have been recorded in the country.
It warned that infections may surge as another wave of cases could be experienced in two weeks following the flooding brought by heavy rains on Aug. 29 to 30.

articles.title: ICC prosecutor opposes ‘reframed’ charges vs Duterte
articles.summary: The International Criminal Court prosecutor has opposed the defense’s request to reframe the crimes against humanity charges against former president Rodrigo Duterte, saying the issues it…

blocks.text: September 13, 2026 | 12:00am
ICC acting prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutor has opposed the defense’s request to reframe the crimes against humanity charges against former president Rodrigo Duterte, saying the issues it raised had already been settled during the confirmation proceedings.
In a 10-page response, ICC acting prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang urged Trial Chamber III to dismiss the motion filed by Duterte’s defense questioning the form of the charges.
Defense lawyer Peter Haynes, in a motion dated Aug. 31, argued that the original document containing the charges, or DCC, “is not fit for purpose and should be struck out.”

Haynes said the charges were improperly framed by grouping the alleged crimes under three topical headings, supposedly violating Duterte’s right to be informed in detail of the nature, cause and content of the charges against him.
The defense asked Trial Chamber III to direct the ICC prosecutor to file an updated DCC before the Pre-Trial Chamber that confirmed the charges against Duterte.
Niang, however, said the defense failed to distinguish between the legal adequacy of the charges and the accused’s right to notice.
He also said many of the defense’s arguments had already been addressed during the confirmation proceedings.

“Questions as to the form of charges are a matter for confirmation proceedings, not trial. The defense fully participated in the substantive proceedings to confirm the charges, up to and including seeking leave (unsuccessfully) to appeal the Pre-Trial Chamber’s confirmation decision on the issue of the form of the charges,” Niang wrote.

Duterte is facing crimes against humanity charges involving three sets of alleged incidents: murders in Davao from 2013 to 2016, murders of high-value targets from 2016 to 2017 and murders and attempted murders linked to barangay operations from 2016 to 2018.
Niang rejected the defense’s criticisms of how the charges were structured, saying the three counts “each have a clear temporal, geographical and material scope.”
On the issue of notice, Niang maintained that the prosecution had provided the defense with sufficient information about the incidents and victims that would be covered during the trial.

“The prosecution has duly provided sufficient notice of all the relevant incidents and victims, both through the information provided in the course of confirmation proceedings but also through auxiliary pre-trial documents such as the trial brief,” he added.
Duterte’s trial is expected to begin on Nov. 30.

articles.title: P31.2 billion available to fill 64,530 teaching posts – DBM
articles.summary: The Department of Education and Department of Budget and Management have clarified reports that the proposed 2027 national budget provides “zero funding” for the hiring of public school…

blocks.text: September 13, 2026 | 12:00am

The two agencies clarified that while the national expenditure program (NEP) does not propose the creation of another batch of new Teacher I positions, this does not mean that DepEd cannot hire teachers in 2027.
Businessworld / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) and Department of Budget and Management (DBM) have clarified reports that the proposed 2027 national budget provides “zero funding” for the hiring of public school teachers, stressing that P31.22 billion is provided for the filling of 64,530 authorized teaching positions.

Of the 64,530 teaching positions funded for filling, 31,614 are existing vacant teaching positions recorded in the Government Manpower Information System as of April 24, 2026, while another 32,916 teaching positions were newly created and approved by DBM in May 2026.
These authorized positions remain available for DepEd to fill as qualified applicants are hired. They do not expire simply because they are not immediately filled within the year they were created.

DepEd and DBM noted that the 64,530 teaching positions reflected in the proposed 2027 budget are based on the official personnel data available to DBM during the budget preparation process and the applicable cut-off periods.
These comprise 31,614 existing vacant teaching positions recorded in the GMIS as of April 24, 2026 and 32,916 newly created teaching positions subsequently approved by DBM in May 2026.

articles.title: PNP: VP should substantiate claims on threats
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte should substantiate her allegations that she has been receiving threats to her security since 2023, the Philippine National Police said yesterday.

blocks.text: September 13, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte on July 30, 2026.
Inday Sara Duterte via Facebook
MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte should substantiate her allegations that she has been receiving threats to her security since 2023, the Philippine National Police said yesterday.

At a Saturday News Forum in Quezon City, PNP spokesman Col. Allen Rae Co urged Duterte to come forward and give them details about the threats she is allegedly receiving so they could conduct an investigation.

According to Co, the PNP would never threaten her, stressing they are mandated to protect not only the President, who is their commander-in-chief, but also Duterte being the second highest official in the country.
Co said they are also keeping tabs on netizens who have been issuing threats against the government through their social media accounts.
The police spokesman warned the public that even if they locked their profile on Facebook, police investigators can still probe them for their wrongdoing.
“It’s no different from identifying the perpetrators of other crimes,” he said.
After her arraignment for a grave threats case at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court was deferred on Friday, Duterte again mentioned about the threats she is facing from the Marcos administration.
She earlier said she does not trust the courts and the police.
‘Self-serving’
Duterte’s demand for President Marcos to resign is the height of callousness and is every bit self-serving, Bicol Saro Party-list Rep. Terry Ridon said yesterday at the same forum.

Ridon, who serves as a member of the House prosecution in the impeachment trial of Duterte, said there would be no problem and it is even expected from the supporters of the Vice President to call for the resignation of the President.
But for the Vice President herself, as the constitutionally-provided first in the line of succession in case the President is removed from office, Ridon said that was just plain humorous.

“I cannot remember at the height of EDSA Dos or in the time of resident (Rodrigo) Duterte that the vice president, who may benefit from the resignation of the president, actually called for a resignation,” Ridon said.
Ridon said the Vice President should just leave it to her spokespersons or supporters to express these types of sentiments.
Relevant
Lawyer Mans Carpio is highly relevant to the unexplained wealth charge against his wife Sara Duterte because what he owns also has bearing on her wealth, Ridon said.
He said questioning Carpio could help establish the actual extent of the couple’s properties, wealth and business interests.
According to him, the prosecution is therefore keeping open the option of calling Carpio as a hostile witness as it begins presenting evidence on the unexplained wealth charge.

The Senate impeachment court earlier allowed subpoenas for bank and tax records involving Duterte, Carpio and their companies. Prosecutors have since received copies of the documents for use in Article II.
Ridon said prosecutors are reviewing more than 1,800 financial documents for Article II, including bank and tax records involving Duterte, Carpio and their companies.
The prosecution is scheduled to begin on Sept. 14 presenting evidence to prove its allegation that Duterte betrayed public trust for arising from alleged unexplained wealth. — Daphne Galvez

articles.title: Senate: 11 votes, not 10, needed on threshold
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court will need 11 votes from the active roster of 20 senator-judges to overturn the ruling setting the conviction threshold at 16 votes in the impeachment trial of Vice…

blocks.text: September 13, 2026 | 12:00am
Senator-judges are set to vote on Sept. 23 on the conviction threshold of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment.
Senate File Photo

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court will need 11 votes from the active roster of 20 senator-judges to overturn the ruling setting the conviction threshold at 16 votes in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, a court official clarified yesterday.

Speaking over radio dwIZ yesterday, impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol corrected his earlier statement that only 10 votes would be needed, an error that was carried in headlines, including in The STAR’s banner story released yesterday.
Tongol had said during a Zoom press briefing Friday that Escudero would not vote on the matter because it was his July 6 ruling that was under appeal.
The ruling set the number of votes needed to convict at 16 based on Escudero’s interpretation of the 1987 Constitution’s impeachment clause requiring “two-thirds of all the members of the Senate.”
Escudero and Senate secretary and impeachment clerk of court Renato Bantug Jr. later called Tongol to inform him that he was incorrect and that Escudero’s vote would be counted.

“We saw and monitored the headlines [yesterday]. [On Friday], when I said that, I was only applying my understanding of the parliamentary rules, which are suppletorily applicable, that the president shall not vote on the matter unless his vote is decisive,” Tongol said.

“But I was told by our presiding officer and clerk of court that based on their study, the presiding officer would still vote on the matter. So, if 20 attend, it would need, not 10, but 11 to overturn his ruling,” he added.

With 20 active senator-judges, the court would therefore need a simple majority of 11 affirmative votes on Sept. 23 to overturn Escudero’s ruling and lower the threshold from the current interpretation of 16 votes out of 24 senators to 13 votes out of the 20 active members.
Escudero is expected to defend his position that 16 votes are needed to convict and that “all members” refers to the complete roster of 24 senators, regardless of their legal status.
“We expect his vote to be against the appeal. If he votes otherwise, then there would no longer be a ruling to appeal,” Tongol said.
The threshold issue was raised by Sen. Erwin Tulfo during the Sept. 8 trial, when he moved for the senator-judges to tackle the contentious matter.

Critics, however, questioned whether the Senate impeachment court should decide the issue, arguing that the Supreme Court should interpret what constitutes “all members of the Senate,” given the court’s unusual circumstances.

Four senators are physically absent for various reasons: Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are facing non-bailable plunder cases, Ronald dela Rosa is a fugitive from the International Criminal Court over crimes against humanity allegations and Loren Legarda is on medical leave abroad for a lung condition.
The senator-judges will hear from four amici curiae, or judiciary resource persons, on Sept. 16 to help guide their decision on the threshold issue.
They are retired chief justices Artemio Panganiban, Reynato Puno and Hilario Davide Jr. and retired associate justice Adolf Azcuna. Davide and Azcuna were framers of the 1987 Constitution.

All four “friends of the court” are expected to participate in the briefing, although Davide will submit a legal memorandum instead of attending physically. He previously presided over the aborted impeachment trial of deposed president Joseph Estrada.

articles.title: Romualdez taken to PGH for independent medical check
articles.summary: Leyte representative and former speaker Martin Romualdez was transferred yesterday to the Philippine General Hospital in Manila from Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City to undergo…

blocks.text: September 13, 2026 | 12:00am

Bureau of Jail Management and Penology officers escort an ambulance reportedly carrying former speaker Martin Romualdez as the convoy arrives at the Philippine General Hospital in Manila on September 12, 2026.
Noel Pabalate

MANILA, Philippines — Leyte representative and former speaker Martin Romualdez was transferred yesterday to the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) in Manila from Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City to undergo independent medical and diagnostic tests – as ordered by the Sandiganbayan Third Division – to determine if there is justification for his request for continued hospital detention.

The ambulance carrying Romualdez left Cardinal Santos at 8:11 a.m. and arrived at PGH 24 minutes later at 8:35 a.m. under heavy guard by police officers and personnel of the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP).
“He will undergo medical assessment with PGH to submit its findings and recommendations to the Sandiganbayan,” BJMP spokesman Supt. Jayrex Joseph Bustinera said on Viber.
The results of the tests are expected to be released this afternoon and presented before the Sandiganbayan tomorrow.
Romualdez’s transfer from Cardinal Santos “was safe and orderly,” UP-PGH spokesman Jonas del Rosario said, adding that they have organized a group of specialists to conduct the tests.
In a statement, the PGH said it “will remain objective and professional in conducting the examinations, in accordance to the highest standards of the medical field.”

Dr. Gerardo Legaspi, director of UP-PGH, is set to testify before the Sandiganbayan tomorrow on the hospital’s findings and recommendation. He has also been directed to submit a daily medical report on Romualdez’s condition.
The Leyte congressman, who is first cousin of President Marcos, will stay in PGH until the Sandiganbayan orders his transfer to the New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory in Payatas.
The detention cell awaiting Romualdez can accommodate 10 detainees. It has a floor area of 47 to 50 square meters with five double deck beds, two restrooms and two ceiling fans.
Sens. Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are detained in the same facility, on plunder charges.

Romualdez, facing plunder for allegedly receiving P7.4 billion in kickbacks from promised government projects from 2022 to 2025, was admitted at Cardinal Santos on Sept. 7 an hour before the Sandiganbayan issued a warrant for his arrest.

His was not an emergency case even if he was complaining of chest pains when admitted, Dr. Kurt Allen Sibayan told the Sandiganbayan on Thursday. Romualdez did not go through the emergency but was directly admitted to a private room, where authorities served him the arrest warrant.
A detainee shirt was draped over his hospital gown when the warrant was served, as shown in photos released by the Department of the Interior and Local Government.
The Sandiganbayan on Friday transferred Romualdez’s custody to the BJMP from the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group of the Philippine National Police. — Andrew Ronquillo, Emmanuel Tupas

articles.title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down
articles.summary: Amodei's call comes amid growing concerns that AI models may become able to inflict serious damage worldwide.

blocks.text: The head of leading AI company Anthropic has called for the pace of development of artificial intelligence models to slow down and to be closely monitored.
In an essay on Saturday, Dario Amodei said developing AI was not in question, but the risks associated with it were "serious" and companies and governments must be given time to address them.
He proposed a three-point plan that includes independent monitoring of AI models as they are developed, industry-wide regulation and global regulation.

There have been growing concerns recently about the technology's potential risks - the most serious of which suggested there is a greater than 10% chance it "could kill all humans" within the next decade.
Anthropic previously said it had identified and disrupted attempts to use its AI model for "malicious activity" which could support the development of biological weapons.

But the starkest warning came from two employees from Anthropic's safety team who have resigned in the last two weeks saying humanity may not survive, external the race among AI companies to develop machines that are smarter than humans.

The warnings have prompted calls to action, but US President Donald Trump has so far rejected such fears, saying on Thursday he was concerned "if we don't win AI, we're going to be put in a very bad position".

In his essay, called We Must Pace the Frontier, Amodei pointed out that AI had advanced "drastically faster" including its "ability to build the next generation of AI" - and mentioned an incident involving rival OpenAI which has revealed that agents conducted cybersecurity attacks, external on targets they were not asked to attack in July.
The OpenAI agents had "essentially acted as a fanatically devoted collective", Amodei said.

In its comments about the incident, OpenAI said "the significance of the inter-agent communication activity was not apparent to the leaders" until July and the company was slowing down training of certain advanced AI models and tools as a result, noting that there was now an increased risk of AI tools spiraling out of control.
In his essay, Amodei called for "building AI at a balanced rate that aims to ensure its safety while still achieving its benefits".
This would not mean "halting model training or technical progress, but ensuring companies take adequate time to align and safeguard their models, and for third party evaluators to confirm this".
He was committing Anthropic to this "unilaterally" - as well as calling on governments "to require other frontier companies to match".

In his blog, he recognised that regulation might not be able to keep up with the pace of AI, and therefore called on AI companies to "voluntarily work together to set standard" in parallel with regulation.
The Anthropic CEO went on to address the impact that a slowdown would have on the industry and competition with leading developers worldwide, particularly China.

"I believe that if slowing down bought us even an extra year or two before models reach critical levels of capability, and we used that time to advance alignment, we could greatly reduce the risk that something goes seriously wrong," Amodei said.

This would have to be done in a co-ordinated manner "without sacrificing commercial advantage or the United States' lead in AI". Any slowdown would have to be limited, he said, to avoid allowing China to pull ahead.
He urged the US government to take measures so that US companies' AI chips could not be sold to China - or the technology shared with authoritarian countries.

articles.title: ‘We must slow the pace’: CEO of Anthropic calls for an AI slowdown
articles.summary:
In a social media post, Dario Amodei proposed a plan including third-party evaluations of AI systems

The CEO of the artificial intelligence company

blocks.text: The CEO of the artificial intelligence company Anthropic issued a new appeal on Saturday for the AI industry to “slow down” and offered a three-part plan for doing so, saying that his company would “unilaterally” commit to the first of the steps.

In a post on social media, Dario Amodei shared a link to an essay titled We Must Pace the Frontier in which he lays out how Anthropic would provide “third-party evaluators with permanent, employee-level access to our systems, so that they can verify adherence to our safety measures, report on incidents, and assess models’ alignment during training”.

The move comes after a former Anthropic researcher warned on Wednesday that AI could precipitate human extinction by 2030. Researcher Jacob Coxon said in a series of posts that he had quit his job because Anthropic and his previous employer, OpenAI, were ignoring or mishandling their response to the threat AI posed.

“Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives,” Coxon wrote. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade … No other human activity poses this level of danger.”

An Anthropic spokesperson said in a statement to the Guardian that the company had “always been transparent that AI will bring both enormous benefits and unprecedented risks” and it was building “models with some of the strongest safeguards in the industry”.
Earlier this year, Amodei published a lengthy essay titled The Adolescence of Technology that addressed some of fears surrounding the accelerating technology.
In his latest essay, he said that “carefully wielded, AI can be the latest in a long line of technological miracles that have uplifted and ennobled humanity.

“But like many technologies before it, AI brings risks, and because it is such a powerful technology, these risks are serious … A race to the bottom, spurred by commercial incentives, can make these risks more acute,” he wrote.

But, Amodei continued, “over the last few months, I have become convinced that fully addressing the risks requires even more prudence – not just investing in risk prevention, but pacing the rate of capabilities advancement so that risk prevention has time to keep up.
“We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain,” he added in bold type.
Amodei also wrote that over the summer he’d seen AI “advancing drastically faster”, a dynamic called recursive self-improvement.
“Left unchecked, it could outrun our ability to understand and control these systems, and so must be pursued very carefully, if at all,” he said.

The executive also addressed the recent Hugging Face incident, in which a swarm of AI agents created by OpenAI acted as a “fanatically devoted collective conducting cybersecurity attacks on targets they were not asked to attack”.
after newsletter promotion

Clément Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face, wrote in response to Amodei’s Saturday letter that “it’s now clear that alignment is critical and won’t be solved behind the closed doors of a handful of frontier labs”. Delangue said Hugging Face had asked to be part of Anthropic’s “embedded evaluators” program.
He added: “Let’s make AI safer by making it more transparent!”

The three-step plan Amodei proposes includes building AI “at a balanced rate that aims to ensure its safety” by “ensuring companies take adequate time to align and safeguard their models, and for third party evaluators to confirm this”.

The second step he proposes is to require industry-wide coordination, and the third is to ensure global coordination. “The steps do not need to be taken strictly in order, and some of them may be much harder to achieve than others,” he wrote.

Amodei said he continues “to believe that AI can enormously improve the quality of human life”. But he warned that “the measures I propose to advance the frontier at a safe pace will not be easy. But I believe we owe it to humanity to try.”

Responses to Amodei’s post were mixed across social media, with significant support coming from figures such as OpenAI researcher Aidan McLaughlin, who called the post “excellent” and agreed “with basically every word”, and Elon Musk, who simply said: “Dario is right.”

articles.title: Burial of King Oyo takes place in Uganda as news anchor prepares for throne
articles.summary:
Royal guards carry casket through streets of Fort Portal amid row over appointment of Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma

Uganda’s King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, long the world’s youngest…

blocks.text: Uganda’s King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, long the world’s youngest monarch, has been buried among the tombs of his royal forebears as ⁠his Tooro kingdom looked to put ⁠a bitter succession battle behind ​it.

Oyo’s appointed successor, the news anchor Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, cast nine coffee berries into the grave at the Karambi Royal Tombs, marking the formal handover of power in the western Ugandan kingdom.
Oyo made global headlines in 1995 when he took the throne at the age of three. Images of the toddler king wearing a crown and royal robes sparked curiosity and adoration around the world.

blocks.caption: King Oyo of the Toro kingdom was for a long time the world’s youngest monarch. Photograph: Sipa/Shutterstock

blocks.text: He died last month at 34 ⁠in the United States, where he was receiving treatment for cancer.
Uganda is led by an elected head of state but retains several kingdoms that pre-date the ​British colonial era and are regarded as bulwarks of traditional identity ‌and heritage.
At a church service before ‌the burial, Oyo, who became a UN goodwill ambassador championing the fight against HIV and Aids, was eulogised as a reserved but jovial young man.
“Although ‌he became king and carried responsibilities far beyond what most people ever experience, he never completely lost the young boy who loved to have fun,” said his sister, Ruth Komuntale.

Royal guards clad in orange shawls then led the hearse carrying Oyo’s casket through the streets of the kingdom’s capital, Fort Portal, to the royal tombs, as thousands of mourners joined the procession on foot.
The burial, which was held 31 years to the day after Oyo’s coronation, followed days of bickering within the notoriously fractious royal family.
A committee consisting of members ‌of the royal clan announced on Wednesday it had chosen Oyo’s cousin, Kijanangoma, a news anchor and editor at state broadcaster UBC, as king.

But the late king’s immediate family said his hitherto unknown son should succeed him, as called ​for in his will. Oyo never married and was not known to have any children until the kingdom’s prime minister said in the statement announcing his death that he had a son.

blocks.caption: UBC news anchor Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma. Photograph: UBC Uganda

blocks.text: Supporters of Kijanangoma’s succession say Oyo’s family has not been able to produce basic information about the purported son.

A source with knowledge of crisis talks over the matter said Ugandan authorities had successfully pushed through Kijanangoma’s succession on Friday. A government spokesperson could not be reached for comment.
The archbishop of the ⁠Church of Uganda, Stephen Kaziimba Mugalu, called for unity.
“Words spoken in grief can cause pain, division and conflict,” he ​told mourners. “It can even destroy the legacy ​of the king we are mourning.“
Oyo himself took the throne after a protracted succession battle that finished in court.

In ​addition to his ceremonial responsibilities and campaigning ‌against HIV and Aids, ​Oyo cultivated close ties with former ​Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, whom he named a special adviser to the monarch. Gaddafi donated money towards refurbishment of the royal palace.
The 56-year-old Kijanangoma, who maintained a lower profile as the succession battle played out, has been described by fellow Ugandan journalists as quiet and humble.
Besides the throne, the new king will inherit a considerable royal estate including swathes of land and sizeable cash payouts from the central government.

articles.title: Ukraine: Several killed in series of Russian strikes
articles.summary: Local authorities said several civilians were killed and dozens more wounded across Ukraine by Russian strikes. Meanwhile, the Kremlin has rejected Volodymyr Zelenskyy's proposal to meet with the…

image.caption: Dozens of people were injured in a Russian attack on a residential area in OdessaImage: Nina Liashonok/REUTERS

blocks.text: Russia continued on Saturday its constant strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure, killing at least four people and wounding dozens more.

According to Ukrainian officials, two people were killed in the southern Zaporizhzhia region, while steelmaker ArcelorMittal reported that two more people were killed at its plant in Kryvyi Rih, a city in the center of the country.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also said that a Russian strike on an apartment building in Odesa wounded 37 people and that rescue teams are searching for two missing individuals.

blocks.caption: The southern Ukrainian port city of Odesa is a frequent target of Russian attacksImage: State Emergency Service of Ukraine in Odesa Region/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: He added that ten regions came under Russian attack last night and that Russian attack drones are still flying over many of them.
Ukraine retaliates by hitting chemical plants

In response to Russian attacks, Kyiv is fighting back. According to Zelenskyy, Ukraine has attacked "chemical enterprises" in the Perm region of the Urals and in the Samara region, which is located southwestern Russia.

The General Staff in Kyiv also reported a fire at a rubber factory in Togliatti, located in the Samara region. According to their statement, the company specializes in producing synthetic rubber important for tactical and ballistic missiles.
Togliatti Mayor, Ilya Sukhih, said that one person was hospitalized following a massive attack on the city. He added that several multi-story residential buildings were damaged.
Kremlin rebuffs Zelenskyy's meeting proposal

In an exclusive interview with DW, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he is willing to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Group of 20 (G20) leaders' summit in Miami in December.
Zelenskyy backs Putin meeting at Miami G20: 'Results matter'

However, on Saturday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that Moscow has yet to decide whether Putin will travel to the summit. "We don't know yet ​whether we'll be going to ​Miami," Peskov said, according to Russian media.
Commenting on Zelenskiy's proposal, Peskov reiterated Moscow's longstanding position that if the Ukrainian leader wants to meet with the Russian leader, he should come to Moscow.

articles.title: Donations of £72m make Reform’s prospects both rosier and riskier
articles.summary:
Party can boost its campaign power with funds from billionaire backers, but it can also lose support from ordinary Britons

All things being equal, pretty much any political strategist would…

blocks.text: All things being equal, pretty much any political strategist would welcome a £72m war chest; a sum higher than the combined spending of every major party at the 2024 general election. But all things are not equal, and with such a huge amount comes risk.

Reform UK has been vocal in its arguments that two sudden £36m windfalls from billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne merely “levels the playing field” with the bigger parties when it comes to funding.

In one sense this carries some weight. Of the £65m-ish spent in 2024 by the Labour, Conservative, Liberal Democrat, Green and Reform parties, less than a 1oth was used by Nigel Farage’s party. Labour’s fighting fund was more than five times bigger.

But these are unprecedented sums, donated at an unlikely time – an election is almost three years away even if Reform is convinced that Andy Burnham could seek his own personal mandate as early as next May.

The donations give Reform huge scope to expand its electoral machine. They could fund the employment of a new staff member in every UK constituency until the election, though their impact is magnified by the fact that parties devote resources to a much smaller number of target seats.

So, what is the downside? There are two. The first is that every time Farage presents Reform as the voice of ordinary Britons, his opponents can argue it is in reality the plaything of people who are wealthy and disconnected from everyday life to a degree almost unimaginable to most voters.

Delo and Harborne are strikingly similar: cryptocurrency billionaires who are either based overseas – Harborne in Thailand, although he is electorally registered in the UK – or formerly so – Delo recently returned to the UK from Hong Kong.

Opponents will also make much of the fact that Reform’s pledges to liberalise crypto rules in the UK appear likely to make both men even richer, even though the party argues this was its stance before it attracted such donors.

The second, and arguably bigger, concern for Reform is the renewed focus this places on Farage’s own finances, and the perceived cloud of sleaze which has in recent months become more dense around both him and the party.

As well as donating large sums to Reform previously, Harborne also gave £5m to Farage, a gift that Farage failed to declare on entering parliament, and which is being investigated by the parliamentary standards watchdog as a potential breach of MPs’ rules.

Farage only disclosed the gift when the Guardian revealed it in April, prompting not just the standards investigation and the slightly quixotic byelection he fought to supposedly clear his name, but a subsequent period when the Reform leader skipped his previous timetable of regular press conferences to avoid awkward questions.

Things became even worse for Farage on the eve of Reform’s annual conference a week ago when undercover footage broadcast by Channel 4 News seemingly showed senior Reform officials trying to avoid electoral laws on foreign donations, with Farage himself apparently informed.

The party has denied any wrongdoing, but two key Farage aides – Dan Jukes, his de facto chief of staff, and James Orr, Reform’s head of policy – have been suspended, and police are investigating any potential wrongdoing.

Optimistic Reform officials might argue privately that £72m could buy enough advertising to blitz any negative coverage, and it is notable how senior figures, such as the deputy leader, Richard Tice, insist the party is“at war” with traditional media.

But is is more complex than that, especially under Westminster’s first-past-the-post electoral system. If a party hopes to win it must not only convince its base to turn out and vote, but not be so toxic so that other voters unite to stop it.
Polls show increasing numbers of voters see Reform and its leader as not just undesirable but shifty, even dishonest, and they are willing to vote however is necessary to stop Farage entering No 10.
Will another £72m in donations from extremely rich men make such perceptions worse? Very possibly. And is that something Reform could do without? Definitely.

articles.title: Celine Dion's return to the stage draws thousands of ecstatic fans to Plenitude Arena in Paris

image.caption: Fanny Sucheyre wears her wedding dress on the way into Dion's show. (Sarah Leavitt/CBC)

blocks.text: Canada·New

Thousands of devoted fans flocked to the Paris suburb of Nanterre on Saturday as Celine Dion returned to the stage for her first full concert in six years, opening a sellout Paris residency after a battle with a rare neurological disorder sidelined her career.
Dion, 58, kicks off sellout residency after stiff person's syndrome diagnosis
Céline mania in Paris ahead of Canadian star's sold-out comeback tour

As the sun began to set in the Paris suburb of Nanterre on Saturday, concertgoers made their way through thousands of feet of barricades, past security and into Europe's largest indoor concert venue. They wore anything from jeans and graphic T-shirts to sparkly mini skirts and floor-length gowns.
For Céline Dion, one woman wore her wedding dress.
"I cancelled the party with all my family and friends to come see Céline," said Fanny Sucheyre, who celebrated her one-year wedding anniversary at the concert.
"I said to myself, if one day I had the chance to see her, I would wear my best dress. So it's my most beautiful dress."

Thousands of devoted fans travelled to Nanterre's Plenitude Arena to watch Dion return to the stage for her first full concert in six years. The show opens a sellout Paris residency after a battle with a rare neurological disorder sidelined Dion's career.
Outside the venue, fans belted out lyrics in both French and English. Several said they had loved the Canadian singer since childhood.
Inside, special edition Céline champagne glasses sold out within minutes and the lines for champagne itself stretched more than 30 metres. Even the men's washroom had snaking line ups.

"It's a dream. I haven't slept for three days. I'm 50 years old and right now I feel like I'm 15," said Guylene Richardson, heading into the arena with her daughter, both in Dion concert tees. "With [Dion's] disease, I didn't think she would come back, so it's great. I'm really happy for her. I'm happy for us."

One of the best-selling artists of all time, she announced a diagnosis of stiff person’s syndrome — which causes stiffness and muscle spasms — and disappeared from the spotlight in 2022. She broke her hiatus to perform Edith Piaf's Hymne à l'amour from the Eiffel Tower during the opening ceremony of the 2024 Paris Olympic Games.

Dion is scheduled to perform a series of 26 concerts over the next eight months. The City of Light has buzzed with anticipation for the singer's comeback, with signs dotting the length of the Champs-Élysées or along the famed river Seine.
With files from Sarah Leavitt and Carly Thomas

articles.title: French officials investigate if 'malicious act' caused train derailment
articles.summary: Officials say a rail fragment was found on the tracks after Friday's crash of a passenger train that left 44 people injured.

blocks.text: Officials in northern France are investigating if the derailment of a passenger train on Friday evening was the result of "a malicious act".
Prosecutor Sébastien Gallois said on Saturday that a fragment of rail had been found on the tracks - and the reasons for its presence were "unknown".
Local media say 186 passengers were on board the train that was operating between Rouen and Caen in Normandy.
Fourty-four were treated for injuries, including an 18-year-old woman who was airlifted to hospital in a critical condition.
Some 140 firefighters and other emergency teams were deployed to the scene of the incident near Cléon, just south of Rouen, shortly before 20:00 (18:00 GMT).
"Suddenly there were a few jolts, and then after about three seconds it got stronger and stronger," Louis, a passenger on the train, told ICI Normandie radio.
"I couldn't stay in my seat anymore. The windows partially shattered, the stones from the track came into the carriage. It was really shocking. I'm still shaking," he added.
The Rouen prosecutor's office said the train driver had tested negative for drugs and alcohol.

articles.title: Six Nigerians extradited to US over $6M online romance scam
articles.summary:
Alleged members of Black Axe criminal network that swindled US women out of $6m flown from South Africa

Six Nigerian nationals linked to an organized criminal network that allegedly swindled…

blocks.text: Six Nigerian nationals linked to an organized criminal network that allegedly swindled American women out of more than $6m through online romance scams were extradited to the United States on Friday.

South African police confirmed they were to be extradited earlier on Friday, while local news in Africa confirmed that the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, known as the Hawks, facilitated their handover to officials from the US Federal Bureau of Investigation and Secret Service at Cape Town international airport, in collaboration with Interpol South Africa.
The men, who were arrested in the South African city of Cape Town in 2021, face wire fraud and money laundering charges.

They are accused of belonging to a criminal network known as the Black Axe, which Interpol describes as being among criminal groups responsible for a significant share of the world’s cyber-enabled financial fraud, typically through romance, cryptocurrency and investment scams.
According to South African police, the men are alleged to have targeted more than 100 women in the US, defrauding them of more than $6m through online romance or love scams.
Among the alleged victims were pensioners and businesspeople who were reportedly targeted through sophisticated online relationships.

“Through the coordination of Interpol South Africa, the six will today be transported from a correctional facility in Cape Town to Cape Town international airport, where they will be handed over to officials from the FBI and the United States Secret Service, who arrived in South Africa this morning,” said police spokesperson Katlego Mogale.

A recent operation by Interpol targeting west African organized crime groups led to the arrest of 58 people and the identification of 263 suspects linked to various criminal networks involved in similar crimes, the multinational police body said last month.
The operation aimed to disrupt money laundering, identify high-value targets, seize assets, and support arrests and prosecution.
In South Africa, authorities raided seven locations in the city of Johannesburg linked to a syndicate that ran romance and investment scams targeting retirees in English-speaking countries.
In that operation in South Africa, police arrested 39 people, seized $2.67m and froze more than 250 bank accounts, Interpol said.

articles.title: Jeremy Thomas, British producer of The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, dies aged 77
articles.summary:
Thomas was noted for collaborations with directors including Bernardo Bertolucci and David Cronenberg

Jeremy Thomas, the distinguished British producer of films including Sexy Beast,…

blocks.text: Jeremy Thomas, the distinguished British producer of films including Sexy Beast, High-Rise and the multi-Oscar-winning The Last Emperor, has died aged 77.
A representative for Thomas said he died on Friday “peacefully, at his country home in Oxfordshire, surrounded by his family and loved ones”.

Thomas, who started producing feature films in the early 1970s, was known for forging strong creative relationships with acclaimed auteurs, producing a string of films directed by the likes of Nicolas Roeg, David Cronenberg and Bernardo Bertolucci.

The Last Emperor, directed by Bertolucci, was an early triumph for Thomas, winning nine Oscars including best picture. He went on to become a major figure in the British film-making establishment, including a spell as chair of the British Film Institute and winning a Bafta for outstanding British contribution to cinema.

Born in 1949, Thomas’s father, Ralph, was a prolific film director whose work included the popular Doctor in the House series starring Dirk Bogarde, and his uncle Gerald Thomas directed all 30 of the Carry On films. Thomas started out as an assistant editor, working on the Jimmy Cliff thriller The Harder They Come and Ken Loach’s Family Life, before gaining his first producer credit on Mad Dog Morgan in 1976, with Dennis Hopper as the 19th-century Australian outlaw of the title.

Thomas was quickly into his stride, making Bad Timing, Significance and Eureka with Roeg, The Shout with Jerzy Skolimowski and Merry Christmas, Mr Lawrence with the Japanese master director Nagisa Oshima. The success of The Last Emperor, which Thomas had to finance independently, consolidated his status as a leading figure in British cinema, and he subsequently concentrated on prestige projects including The Sheltering Sky and Little Buddha (both with Bertolucci) and Naked Lunch (with Cronenberg).

Thomas then suggested to Cronenberg he should direct JG Ballard’s Crash, and the resulting film was enormously controversial, resulting in local authority bans in several areas in the UK. Following this, Thomas’s films included riskier propositions, such as Sexy Beast, directed by Jonathan Glazer, an adaptation of Alexander Trocchi’s Young Adam, by David Mackenzie, and Terry Gilliam’s bizarre corpse comedy Tideland. Later highlights were Jim Jarmusch’s vampire fantasy Only Lovers Left Alive, another Ballard adaptation, High-Rise, directed by Ben Wheatley, and Tale of Tales and Dogman from the Italian director Matteo Garrone.

In 2019 Thomas was the subject of a documentary by Mark Cousins, who accompanied him on his car drive from the UK to the Cannes film festival for another Garrone film, Pinocchio; it screened there in 2021. Thomas also directed one film himself: All the Little Animals, starring Christian Bale, which was released in 1999. His most recent film, Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo, directed by Takashi Miike, is due to premiere at the Toronto film festival on Monday.

articles.title: Ombudsman: Philippines should secure extradition treaties with European countries
articles.summary: Following reports that former Ako Bicol party-list congressman Zaldy Co is hiding in France, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday said it was time for the Philippines to secure extradition…

blocks.text: Published September 12, 2026 10:00pm

Following reports that former Ako Bicol party-list congressman Zaldy Co is hiding in France, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday said it was time for the Philippines to secure extradition treaties with European countries.
Aside from Co, Senator Loren Legarda and her son, Batangas Representative Leandro Leviste—both the subjects of plunder investigations before the Ombudsman—are also in France.
Speaking on dzRH, Remulla lamented the lack of an extradition treaty between the Philippines and France.

Remulla said Co, who is facing criminal charges over his alleged involvement in the flood control mess, was even able to buy an apartment on Avenue Montaigne in France. The Ombudsman also commented that Legarda, who is currently on medical leave, did not appear to want to return home.

“I think we should. At saka maraming Filipino doon,” Remulla said when asked whether he thought the Philippines should pursue more bilateral agreements or extradition treaties with European countries.
(I think we should. And there are many Filipinos there.)

Remulla is scheduled to travel to France, where he plans to meet with several international law enforcement agencies, including the Financial Action Task Force (FATF). He said he hopes to raise his concern that Europe could be turning into a hiding place for individuals facing criminal cases in the Philippines.
“They protect human rights. But will they protect white-collar criminals and those who got their money from corruption and are storing it within the country?” Remulla said.
His brother, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla, is also scheduled to travel to France to meet with Interpol officials.
The Ombudsman may also travel to Brussels or The Hague in the Netherlands to meet with representatives from the European Union.

Remulla made no promises that he would return home with Co. However, his younger brother, Jonvic Remulla, expressed confidence that he could bring Co back to the Philippines. —Jean Mangaluz/VBL, GMA News

articles.title: IDF soldier filmed shooting Palestinian in leg amid West Bank settler standoff
articles.summary:
Incident is latest to raise questions over Israel’s ability or willingness to stop violent settlers in occupied territory

An Israeli soldier shot a Palestinian man, wounding him in the leg,…

blocks.text: An Israeli soldier shot a Palestinian man, wounding him in the leg, as settlers confronted villagers by grazing livestock on Palestinian-owned land in the town of Faqqua in the occupied West Bank.

Eyewitnesses said that a group of settlers had entered the area with their livestock, prompting residents to try to stop them. Israeli forces then intervened and, according to men at the scene, opened fire at residents. One of them shot Qassem Hussam, a Palestinian man in his mid-30s, wounding him in the leg.
Reached by the Guardian, the IDF confirmed it had received a report of the incident and that the person who fired was one of its soldiers.

“Earlier today [Saturday], a report was received regarding friction between Israeli civilians and Palestinians near the area of Faqqua,” the IDF said. “An IDF force that was at the scene fired into the air and toward a Palestinian.”
Mohammed al-Sheikh, 34, who was standing next to Hussam, told the Guardian the confrontation began when villagers encountered Israeli settlers grazing livestock on Palestinian-owned land.

“Then the Israeli soldiers came,” al-Sheikh said. “They started shooting. One soldier shot Hussam and he fell to the ground. We immediately went to help him and move him away. We couldn’t get an ambulance to the area, so we took him to hospital in a private car.”
Hussam was taken to hospital in a light-to-moderate condition, according to the Palestine Red Crescent.

The Israeli military said the incident was being reviewed by commanders and that its findings would be forwarded to the relevant authorities for examination. The IDF added that the military was investigating the soldier who shot the Palestinian man, apparently in breach of army protocol, according to the Times of Israel.
Video of the incident shows a group of Israeli soldiers and settlers confronting unarmed Palestinian men before shots are fired.
The incident is the latest to raise questions over the Israeli government’s ability or willingness to curb violent settlers in the occupied West Bank, where attacks have continued to increase.

On 8 September, the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, said he would “not stand by” as horrific suffering continued, writing in the Guardian that for too long the UK had been hesitant to act, “fearful of being accused of being anti-Israel”.

Ed Miliband, the UK’s foreign secretary, said the government would now take the official position that Israel’s occupation of the West Bank was unlawful in its entirety, and announced sweeping sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements.

The dramatic shift in the UK’s position came after a summer of intense diplomacy against a backdrop of rising settler violence in the West Bank, which led 12 countries, including France and Canada, to announce sanctions.

After Miliband described violent Jewish settler activity in the occupied West Bank as “ethnic cleansing” carried out with the tacit backing of the government of the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, announced retaliatory measures including the closure of the consulate and entry bans on several MPs.
It marked the latest stage in a rapidly worsening dispute between the two countries, with diplomatic relations at their lowest point in years, even as violence in the West Bank has continued.

Israeli forces also carried out raids across Jenin governorate on Saturday, arresting six people and injuring a 14-year-old boy, who suffered a broken hand, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa. Soldiers also raided several villages around Jenin, while forces entered at least five towns in Bethlehem governorate and set up a checkpoint at Za’atara.
East of Ramallah, Israeli settlers attacked the outskirts of Burqa, throwing stones at homes and vehicles.

On 4 September, two Palestinian teenagers were shot dead in al-Mughayyir after settlers entered the village under police and military escort and took dozens of sheep from a Palestinian home, residents and Israeli activists said.
The victims were Khalil Abu Alia, 16, and Omar al-Nassan, 19. Three other pupils from their 470-strong school had already been killed by Israeli soldiers and settlers this year.

According to the UN’s Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), more than 1,111 Palestinians, including at least 243 children, have been killed in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, since 7 October 2023.

articles.title: Bolick redeems self, Ahanmisi catches fire as Gilas Pilipinas rips Kazakhstan in Asian Games
articles.summary: Robert Bolick and Jerrick Ahanmisi spearhead Gilas Pilipinas' scoring spree from three-point range as the defending champions earn their first win in the Asian Games and boost their chances of…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Robert Bolick rebounded from a scoreless outing, while Jerrick Ahanmisi shot the lights out as Gilas Pilipinas claimed its first win in the Asian Games, dealing Kazakhstan a 109-78 beating at the Aichi International Arena in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday, September 12.

Held scoreless in a narrow 89-85 loss to Bahrain the day prior, Bolick fired 20 points in just a little over 15 minutes to help the defending champion Philippines improve to an even 1-1 record in Group C and boost its chances of advancing to the quarterfinals.

Ahanmisi, meanwhile, erupted for a game-high 22 points on a 7-of-11 clip from beyond the arc, torching the Kazakhs in a fourth-quarter scoring spree that allowed the Filipinos to break the game wide open.
Gilas Pilipinas held a slim 18-15 lead at the end of the opening period before Bolick took charge and scattered 13 points in the second frame as it mounted a 50-37 halftime advantage.

Ahanmisi then picked up where Bolick left off, knocking down five three-pointers in the fourth quarter and singlehandedly outscoring the entire Kazakhstan team, which managed just 12 points in the final period of the 31-point blowout.

Calvin Oftana, who erupted for 31 points in the loss to the Bahrainis, still made his presence felt with 12 points, while Sedrick Barefield contributed 11 points, 5 assists, and 4 rebounds as he redeemed himself after going scoreless last game.
Zavier Lucero also delivered a near double-double outing of 10 points and 9 rebounds in the win, which saw the Filipinos sink 16 of their 29 attempts from long range for a healthy 55% shooting.
Bolick and Barefield, who both went 0-of-5 from three-point land against Bahrain, made 4 and 3 triples, respectively, this time around.

One of the few bright spots last game before he tweaked his right ankle late in the fourth quarter, Adrian Nocum played just a little under 16 minutes against the Kazakhs, contributing 4 points and 3 assists.
Anton Bykov produced 15 points and 10 rebounds to show the way for Kazakhstan, which fell to 0-2 after also absorbing a 38-point drubbing from China.
Given a one-day break, the Philippines turns its attention to unbeaten China in its last game of the group stage on Monday, September 14, with a win sending the Filipinos to the quarterfinals.
Only the top two teams from each of the three groups and the two best third-place teams will reach the knockout rounds.
Philippines 109 – Ahanmisi 22, Bolick 20, Oftana 12, Barefield 11, Lucero 10, Baltazar 6, Arana 6, Abarrientos 6, Trollano 5, Nocum 4, Ganuelas-Rosser 4, Bates 3.
Kazakhstan 78 – Bykov 15, Marat 12, Maydekin 12, Neff 11, Rabchenyuk 9, Murzagaliyev 8, Fedchenko 7, Ivanov 2, Sakhipov 2, Severgin 0, Marchuk 0, Kuanov 0.

articles.title: Marcos taps Indian rail firm for Mindanao, Cebu, PNR projects
articles.summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. met with an Indian railway company on Saturday to explore studies for three proposed railway systems in the Philippines, including projects in Mindanao and…

blocks.text: Published September 12, 2026 9:28pm

President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. met with an Indian railway company on Saturday to explore studies for three proposed railway systems in the Philippines, including projects in Mindanao and Cebu and the extension of the Philippine National Railways (PNR) from Tutuban in Manila.
The meeting took place during the 8th BRICS Summit in India.

BRICS is an association of developing economies, of which the Philippines is not a member. Marcos said in his departure message that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi invited him to attend the summit as the 2026 ASEAN chair and as an outreach participant, or a non-member country invited to join the summit discussions.
In a “24 Oras Weekend” report by Darlene Cay, Marcos arrived in India at 11:15 p.m. New Delhi time.
Marcos said he would advocate for global governance, disaster preparedness and international cooperation during the summit.

“We will call for fairer global governance, stronger disaster preparedness, and responsible use of new technologies, climate action and the peaceful settlement of disputes under international law,” Marcos said.

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin also attended the BRICS Summit. However, the Department of Foreign Affairs said Marcos would not hold formal dialogues with either leader.
Marcos said he wanted to ensure that the Philippines remained open to engaging with various countries while upholding international law and responsible conduct in maritime areas.
“We must now ensure that the sea lanes are just as free, open, and governed by law, rules, and responsible behavior,” Marcos said.

The President also met with representatives of the Indian Space Research Organisation and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, which shared insights on disaster management and resilience.

“The meeting was about the experiences of coalition members in dealing with disasters and how to become more disaster-resilient. At the same time, they will also help us access financing,” Presidential Communications Office Secretary Dave Gomez said.

According to Cay’s report, Marcos was also scheduled to meet with Modi to assess the progress of the five-year plan of action between the Philippines and India. It would be their first meeting since Marcos’ state visit to India last year.

“Our discussions will cover defense and maritime cooperation, trade and investment, the proposed preferential trade agreement, health and pharmaceuticals, digital cooperation, tourism, direct air connectivity, and people-to-people ties,” Marcos said.
“It will also be an auspicious occasion to renew our invitation for Prime Minister Modi to visit Manila for the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit in November,” he added.
Marcos was scheduled to attend the BRICS Gala Dinner on the evening of September 12 and deliver a speech during the opening session on September 13.— Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Donald Trump says he would ‘love’ to see united Ireland
articles.summary:
US president say on visit to republic that unification will happen eventually so ‘may as well happen now’

•

blocks.text: Donald Trump has said he would “love” to see a united Ireland and that it “may as well happen now”.

The US president appeared to endorse the push for constitutional change on the island at the start of a two-day visit to Ireland on Saturday. The unexpected intervention prompted a swift rebuttal from the UK government and Northern Ireland’s unionist leaders.

“I don’t want ⁠to cause any problems, ​but ‌I will ‌tell you, I’d love ‌to see it unified,” Trump told reporters at joint press conference with the taoiseach, Micheál Martin, in Dublin. “I think it would be a great feather in everybody’s cap if that happened. You know what? The way I look at it, it’s going to happen eventually. It may as well happen now.”

The unification of Northern Ireland with the republic of Ireland would be “fantastic”, Trump said. “The UK will have something to say about it, obviously. But I think it would be a great thing. I mean, how can it be bad?”

blocks.caption: Micheál Martin welcomes Donald Trump to Farmleigh House, in Dublin, during his trip to the Republic of Ireland. Photograph: Ben Birchall/PA

blocks.text: The intervention jolted his hosts and came two weeks after Andy Burnham said a referendum on unification was “off the table”, which angered Sinn Féin and other Irish nationalists.

Speaking later on Saturday, Trump acknowledged that his comments on unification, made in response to a reporter’s question, would be controversial. “No matter what you say or how you say it, there’s no good answer,” he said. “I gave a nice answer, I think. We’ll worry about it tomorrow.” Unification, he added, would be a “very cool thing”.
A Downing Street spokesperson said the prime minister still believed there was not the required support for unification to trigger a referendum, as set out in the Good Friday agreement.
Gavin Robinson, the Democratic Unionist party (DUP) leader, said Northern Ireland’s constitutional future would be decided by its people, not by commentary in London, Dublin or Washington.

“Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom because that is the settled democratic will of its people. I am confident Northern Ireland will continue to choose the UK and the security it offers. As unionists we are not interested in the destruction of our country by joining with the Irish republic.”

Colum Eastwood, an MP and former leader of the Social Democratic and Labour party (SDLP), and frequent critic of Trump, posted a clip of the president’s remarks on social media and wrote: “Always liked him.”

The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, said: “President Trump is shooting from the hip as usual, just like he did with Greenland and Canada becoming the 51st state. This sort of loose talk about the future of democratic countries is deeply unhelpful and creates unnecessary tension.”

blocks.caption: Demonstrators protesting against Trump’s visit in Dublin. Photograph: Natalia Campos/Reuters

blocks.text: Trump’s comments strayed from predecessors who sought to keep the White House neutral on Ireland’s constitutional future, but the off-the-cuff nature of the remarks suggested there was no change in US policy.

Trump’s unofficial visit is centred on golf – he flew on Saturday afternoon to his resort in Doonbeg, County Clare, which is hosting the Irish Open – but started with a courtesy call in Dublin to Áras an Uachtaráin, the official residence and workplace of the Irish president, Catherine Connolly.

Before her election to the ceremonial post last year, Connolly called Trump a bully and criticised his policies in Gaza and Iran. Their brief encounter, behind closed doors, appeared to go smoothly despite a coded critique of White House policies.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Donald Trump and Catherine Connolly at her presidential residence in Phoenix Park, Dublin. Photograph: Tony Maxwell/PA

blocks.text: Connolly said in a statement afterwards that she “conveyed the strong view of the Irish people that the normalisation of war and genocide can never be accepted” and stressed the importance of the United Nations – an organisation Trump has disparaged. Trump said they had a wide-ranging discussion, including about energy and water, and that Connolly was “terrific”.

Trump held a separate meeting with Martin at the Phoenix Park, where he told the press that Iran would seek peace after the US midterm elections and repeated his claim that his war had prevented Tehran obtaining a nuclear weapon.
Asked about protests against his visit – a large crowd was expected in central Dublin, 5 miles away, as well as at Doonbeg – the president said he had not seen any protests.

blocks.caption: Spectators watch as Air Force One flies Trump over the Irish Open in Doonbeg, County Clare. Photograph: Damien Eagers/PA

blocks.text: Addressing guests as at the US ambassador’s residence, Trump assailed US Democrats as extremists and criticised Europe’s approach to immigration.

He lauded US-Irish relations but reiterated a complaint about the American pharma giants in Ireland. “You took all our medical companies, we’ve got to get a couple of them back. You fleeced us but that’s OK. There’s a lot of room to go around and our relationship with you is fantastic.”
As he left Dublin a crowd at the Garden of Remembrance waved banners and chanted: “Donald Trump, can you hear? We don’t want you here.”
Trump is expected to stay overnight in Doonbeg and present the Irish Open trophy before returning to Washington on Sunday.

articles.title: 10 senators can overturn 16-vote threshold to convict Sara Duterte - Tongol
articles.summary: At least 10 senators can overturn the ruling of Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero that 16 votes are needed to remove Vice President Sara Duterte from office, court…

blocks.text: At least 10 senators can overturn the ruling of Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero that 16 votes are needed to remove Vice President Sara Duterte from office, court spokesperson Regie Tongol said Friday.

Of the 24 senators, four are currently absent, while Escudero would not participate, leaving 19 senators to decide on the matter on September 23, Tongol told reporters. Under a simple majority vote, he said, this means only 10 senators would be needed to overturn the 16-vote threshold for conviction.
“Majority of the quorum present po ang makakaboto. Parang ordinary action lamang po ito ng Senado,” Tongol said.
(The votes of the majority of the quorum present will be the basis. This is just like an ordinary action of the Senate.)

Currently, Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are detained over separate plunder charges, while Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa is in hiding amid an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court (ICC) in connection with the Duterte administration’s war on drugs.
Senator Loren Legarda has not attended the trial for several weeks as she remains abroad on extended medical leave.
However, Tongol said that there is still a possibility that more than the expected 20 senator-judges could be present on voting day.
He also said that in the event of a tie among the senator-judges, the motion on the voting threshold would be considered to have “failed.”
“So the ruling of the presiding officer will stand,” he said.
Speaking to reporters on Friday, Duterte said it had already been decided that the 1987 Constitution would be followed in determining the threshold for conviction.
“So ibig sabihin, ngayon na nagbago 'yung usapan, ibig sabihin ay babaguhin nila. Bakit pa ba natin pag-uusapan 'yun kung hindi naman babaguhin, 'di ba?” she added.
(So that means, now the conversation has changed, it means they will change it. Why are we even talking about it if it’s not going to be changed, right?)
Her brother, Davao City Representative Paolo “Pulong” Duterte, said 10 votes cannot override the Constitution.
"Ten votes to reverse the 16-vote rule? Are you sure about this? Ten votes to change the Constitution? Di puwede (That is not allowed)," he wrote on Facebook on Saturday.

"Ang Constitution mismo ang nagsasabi ng 'two-thirds of all the members of the Senate.' Kung ang bilang ng senators ngayon ay 24, that translates to 16 kasi 'all' ang sabi ng Constitution. Para sa mga law benders natin, baka di niyo alam ang ibig sabihin ng 'all.' Wala yang karugtung na 'all present' or 'all law benders.'"

(The Constitution itself says ‘two-thirds of all the members of the Senate.’ If there are currently 24 senators, that translates to 16 because the Constitution says ‘all.’ For our law benders, perhaps you don’t know what ‘all’ means. There is no qualifier after ‘all’ saying ‘all present’ or ‘all law benders.’")

At the start of the impeachment trial on July 6, Escudero said that under Article XI, Section 3, Paragraph 6 of the 1987 Constitution, no person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of all the members of the Senate.
With the Senate composed of 24 members, Escudero said a literal interpretation of the constitutional provision means a conviction requires at least 16 affirmative votes.
Senator Erwin Tulfo made a manifestation during the September 8 hearing, seeking clarification on the 16-vote threshold, given that four senator-judges are currently not attending the trial.
Tulfo also said it must be clarified whether senators who are detained will be allowed to vote or whether their votes will be accepted by the court even if they are not attending the trial.

To settle the matter, Escudero said the court invited four amici curiae (friends of the court)—retired Supreme Court Chief Justices Hilario Davide, Artemio Panganiban, and Reynato Puno, and former SC Justice Adolf Azcuna—to weigh in on the voting threshold on September 16.
The oral arguments between the defense and prosecution panels, meanwhile, will be held on September 23, with each side given 15 minutes to present its position.
After the oral arguments, the senator-judges are expected to cast their votes. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger
articles.summary: Winemakers can make bubbly up to up to 15% ABV following an unusual harvest that produced sweeter grapes.

blocks.text: The temporary increase in champagne's alcohol content is only expected to affect a small number of wines, a spokeswoman for the Comite Champagne told the BBC.

During the second fermentation process, which gives champagne its bubbles, "a very small number of wines from this harvest could have slightly exceeded the regulatory limit of 13%, reaching around 13.1% or 13.2%".
"Therefore a decision was made to exceptionally and temporarily increase the regulatory limit to 15% - only for this year," she said.
The first grapes were cut in early August and the harvest expanded by the middle of the month, "the earliest ever recorded in Champagne", the association said.

"The 2026 growing season will be remembered as one of the most unusual in Champagne's history, marked by severe spring frosts of historic intensity, an exceptionally early flowering period and five heatwaves throughout the summer." it added.

Speaking in the Times newspaper, Stéphane Vignon, a producer in Verzenay said: "The Mediterranean climate is moving north. This is year one of a new cycle. It's unlikely to be every year, but it will happen again".
Higher-strength champagne is unlikely to be an obvious selling point, warned Jane Anson, a wine columnist and author based in Bordeaux.
She told the Times: "Today people increasingly prefer lower-alcohol
"The battle between what consumers want and what nature provides must be very stressful for producers."
The 2026 vintage is unlikely to hit shelves until 2028 as champagne must age for at least 15 months.
