articles.title: Iraq scrambles to address fallout from alleged militia attack on Saudi oil pipeline
articles.summary: Iraq’s government was racing Saturday to contain the fallout after local Iran-backed militias were accused of attacking and shuttering a key Saudi pipeline.

image.caption: Fighters loyal to the Houthi authorities shout slogans during a rally to recruit more fighters, in Sanaa, Yemen's capital, on Thursday. The country relapsed into war in July after years of calm, drawn into the regional conflict triggered by the U.S.-Israeli offensive against Iran that began Feb. 28.

blocks.text: World·New
Iraq’s government was racing Saturday to contain the fallout after local Iran-backed militias were accused of attacking and shuttering a key Saudi pipeline.
Iran-backed militias deny involvement in strike
· The Associated Press
· Posted: Sep 12, 2026 8:40 AM EDT | Last Updated: 20 minutes ago
Iraq's government was racing Saturday to contain the fallout after local Iran-backed militias were accused of attacking and shuttering a key Saudi pipeline.

Though an umbrella group of Iran-backed militias in Iraq denied their involvement, Iraq's government confirmed the attacks had originated from its territory. The government pledged to investigate and dismissed a military commander.

The country is under mounting pressure to prevent local militias from aiding other Iran proxy groups across the region. The Iraqi government has set a Sept. 30 deadline for non-state groups to disarm, but several of the most powerful militias have said they will not comply.

Pressure to disarm the militias is especially acute as the Iran-backed Houthi rebels make an advance across Yemen’s west coast in a major setback to the Saudi-backed coalition that risks escalating the war in the region. The Houthis on Friday seized an island in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key shipping lane through which about 12 per cent of global trade passes.

Their virtual control of the strait could send global oil prices — already inflated by the six-month Iran-U.S. war — spiralling. The strait has become a vital commercial lane for Saudi oil ever since the Iran war disrupted shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

items: Houthis seize strategic island, Saudis close pipeline as fighting escalates

blocks.text: Asked about the region on Saturday while speaking to reporters in Dublin, U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran was "probably" responsible for the pipeline attack but tried to calm concerns.
He said his administration has "had discussions" with the Houthis, though he did not specify to which talks he was referring.
"The Houthis called us, and they don't want to fight with us," Trump said. "They would much prefer not having us involved, and they're letting most ships go through."
Iraq to investigate attack on Saudi pipeline

A group of Iran-backed militias in Iraq denied in a statement on Saturday that they were responsible for the attacks on the East-West crude oil pipeline in Saudi Arabia, while praising the Houthis for their "ongoing battlefield victories against Saudi forces."
The group said it would co-operate with the Iraqi government's investigation.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said earlier Saturday that he'd ordered an investigation into the operations command of Maysan province, along the border with Iran, and dismissed the province's commander.

Saudi Arabia shut down the major, cross-country oil pipeline on Friday, calling it a "precautionary measure" after the pipeline came under drone attack. It blamed the attacks on several drones that came from Iraq but said the kingdom would not retaliate, to give the Iraqi government "an opportunity to take the necessary measures."
Several Arab countries, including Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Egypt, condemned the attack on Saturday, according to the Saudi state news agency.

items: Iran-backed Houthis attack Saudi oil facilities, injuring dozens

blocks.text: Built in the 1980s, the East-West pipeline has played an important role in Saudi Arabia's ability to export oil following the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war. By early June, Saudi Arabia had more than doubled oil exports from the Red Sea port at the pipeline's end to more than five million barrels per day, according to the International Energy Agency.

Tehran-backed Iraqi militias have carried out strikes on U.S.-linked targets both inside and outside of Iraq since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28, and have co-ordinated with Yemen's Houthi rebels to attack Saudi Arabia.
Iraq closes border crossings with Iran
In a move possibly linked to the investigation, Iraq closed two key border crossings with Iran, Iraq's state-run news agency reported Saturday.
The report said that Iraqi officials were at the border, investigating previous "violations and infractions" at the crossings.

Valiollah Hayati, the deputy governor of Iran's southwestern Khuzestan province, named the closed crossings as Shalamcheh and Chazabeh. They are among the main official border crossings between Iran and Iraq.
Iranian state media said the measure would halt all passenger and commercial traffic through the two crossings until further notice.

Saudi Arabia and the United States bombed Iranian-backed militias in Iraq in July after blaming them for drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities that had been claimed by the Houthis. Regional officials told The Associated Press that the Houthis helped the Iraqi militias plan and execute the attacks.
Fighting threatens to reignite Yemen’s civil war

The escalating fighting threatens to end a fragile truce that had largely halted Yemen's civil war since 2022. At stake are 40 million people in the Arab world's poorest country. The conflict killed 150,000 and brought many others to the brink of famine.
The surge in fighting in the past week has sent more than 46,000 people fleeing, the United Nations migration agency said Friday.

The Houthis have been at war with Yemen's government since 2014, when the rebels seized much of northern and central Yemen and the capital, Sanaa. Saudi Arabia entered the war the following year on the side of the government.

articles.title: Deadly Russian strikes hit Ukraine after Putin's warning to European leaders
articles.summary: Russian strikes killed three civilians and wounded dozens in Ukraine, local officials said Saturday, after Russian President Vladimir Putin warned that sending European troops into Ukraine would…

image.caption: Firefighters work at the site of a gas station that was destroyed after being hit by a Russian drone strike, in Kyiv, Ukraine's capital, on Friday. (Alina Smutko/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Russian strikes killed three civilians and wounded dozens in Ukraine, local officials said Saturday, after Russian President Vladimir Putin warned that sending European troops into Ukraine would amount to direct conflict with Russia.
3 killed and dozens wounded in Russian offensive
· The Associated Press
· Posted: Sep 12, 2026 8:16 AM EDT | Last Updated: 9 minutes ago

Ukraine is under mounting pressure from Russia’s intensifying air campaign that uses ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones to pierce defences. Moscow’s attacks have targeted Ukraine’s power grid ahead of winter in what officials say is meant to demoralize civilians.
Two people were killed and one wounded when Russian drones struck a residential area overnight in the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, regional head Ivan Fedorov said Saturday.
One person died and three others were wounded in strikes on Kryvyi Rih, according to local officials.

In the Black Sea port of Odesa and the surrounding area, 35 people were wounded in what regional head Oleh Kiper called a "massive attack." Among the buildings hit was a residential highrise, whose upper floors were completely destroyed.

items: Zelenskyy describes Canada-U.S. tensions as 'strange,' draws comparison to Ukraine and Russia

blocks.text: Putin, speaking to reporters at the BRICS summit in India on Friday, said that if European governments send troops into Ukraine, it will mean "a war with Russia."
"Now they’re talking about how they’re considering sending troops into Ukraine. That means a war with Russia," he said.
Some European leaders have pledged their commitment to a potential peacekeeping force, a prospect that Moscow has repeatedly described as unacceptable.
Putin denies threat to Europe, despite incursions
Putin also denied Russia posed any threat to Europe, saying "there is no such threat and never has been."
"We do not threaten, nor do we intend to threaten, European countries," he said.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Thursday that two incidents along Ukraine’s borders with Poland and Moldova this week were a preview of potential intensified Russian provocations at Ukraine’s border crossing points with Europe.

items: Canada, Ukraine forge 100-year pact built on drones and defence

blocks.text: Two people died when Russian drones hit the Starokozache border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova on Tuesday night, while a "direct threat" to a Polish-Ukrainian crossing point on Wednesday night was only avoided thanks to co-operation between Warsaw and Kyiv, he said.

Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told Deutsche Welle, in an interview published Saturday, that he would meet Putin if both leaders were invited to the Group of 20 summit of rich and developing nations in December in Miami.

Putin’s foreign policy adviser, Yuri Ushakov, said Saturday that the possibility of Putin attending the summit had not yet been discussed. The Kremlin in the past has said that Zelenskyy can come to Moscow if he wants a meeting with Putin, a proposal Kyiv has rejected.

blocks.text: Bulgarian authorities are investigating a fire at a munitions storage facility operated by arms maker EMCO.
Police say the blaze broke out Friday night and follows a similar incident at another EMCO site in August.
EMCO's munitions are used in Ukraine and sabotage has not been ruled out.
The full extent of the damage is not yet known but no casualties have been reported.
"At present there is no danger to the population," said local police, adding that employees had been evacuated and the area cordoned off.
EMCO has ruled out any chance of human error in the incident.

articles.title: Christopher Harborne matches £36m Reform donation of Ben Delo
articles.summary:
Party leader, Nigel Farage, says he is humbled by the contributions from cryptocurrency billionaires

The cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne has given £36m to Reform UK, matching…

blocks.text: The cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne has given £36m to Reform UK, matching a donation from fellow billionaire Ben Delo.
The pledges are jointly the largest donations made to a UK party and are likely to intensify calls for a cap on political donations.
Reform leader, Nigel Farage, said he was “honoured and humbled” by the donations, which come at a time when Reform is facing intense scrutiny regarding its finances.

The Metropolitan police is conducting an inquiry into Reform’s finances, and Farage is facing a parliamentary standards investigation into a £5m gift from Harborne, made before he was first elected an MP in 2024. Reform UK and Farage have denied any wrongdoing.
Farage said: “I am honoured and humbled that Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne have shown such confidence in Reform.

“Both men know that we are the only party that can turn the country around and win the next general election – thanks to their generosity, we are now able to fight that election on a level playing field.”

Harborne said: “There will be a lot of media speculation regarding this donation. So what do I expect in return for my donations? Nothing. No peerage, no policy change, just a party that is ready for government.

“I have already accumulated enough wealth for the rest of my life. I am committed to putting that to work for Britain and humanity as a whole. I want the same as everyone else in Britain: for my children and grandchildren to have the chance to live happy and productive lives here and be rewarded for their hard work.
“At the next general election people will have to vote for the party that they think will best get that done and I’m making a donation very clearly to the party that I believe will do so.”

articles.title: Trump visits Ireland, says unification would be 'fantastic'
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump's trip to Ireland to watch a golf tournament has also included meetings with leaders there.

image.caption: Trump (in blue suit) received a military welcome upon arrivalImage: Kylie Cooper/REUTERS

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump has said he would "love" to see the Republic of Ireland, an EU member, unite with British-run ⁠Northern Ireland as he faced reporters' questions on a range of issues on Saturday.

Trump is taking the weekend trip largely to watch the Irish Open golf tournament held on a course he owns on the country’s Atlantic coast, but he met as well with the Irish president and prime minister, or taoiseach.
The US leader also spoke optimistically about his country's war with Iran and its trade conflict with Canada, among several other topics.
What did Trump say about Ireland?

After a meeting with Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin in the capital, Dublin, Trump said he very much supported what he said would be the eventual unification of the two parts of the island of Ireland.
"Well, I don't want to ​cause any problems, ​but ‌I will tell you, I'd love to see ‌it unified," Trump told ‌reporters.
"The way I look at it, it's ⁠going ​to happen ​eventually ... I think it would ​be a ‌fantastic thing," he added.
"Now the UK will have ​something ⁠to say about it ... but ⁠I think ​it would be a great thing."

The British government responded swiftly to the remarks, with Prime Minister Andy Burham's office saying that in his view, there was no majority public support for a referendum on the issue and that there would not be another one until that changed.

Previous US presidents have avoided touching on the subject in view of the delicate nature of the issue, with Northern Ireland seeing decades of of deadly sectarian violence in the 20th century over the question of whom it should belong to.

blocks.caption: Micheal Martin (L) has led Ireland twice since 2020Image: Brendan Smialowski/AFP

blocks.text: What did Trump say about the Iran war?
Trump also said that the US war with Iran, which began on February 28, would "end very soon" — a view he has frequently expressed in the past without it becoming reality.
He also said that the end of the conflict would mean that the price of oil, which has soared as a result of the war, would "come tumbling down."
However, he vehemently defended his decision to mount the military operation against Iran.
He said that the US attacked because "Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon", adding: "They were two weeks away from having a nuclear weapon."

"If they had it, they would have blown up Israel, they would have blown up the Middle East, and they would have hit some [...] in my opinion, [of] Europe's cities and beyond cities, and they would probably hit us soon before we put out the fire. But they cannot have a nuclear weapon."
The war with Iran is not supported by a majority of the US population, particularly in view of promises made by Trump on the campaign trail to keep his country out of foreign "forever" conflicts.

blocks.caption: Trump and Martin held talks in Farmleigh House in Phoenix Park in DublinImage: Brendan Smialowski/AFP

blocks.text: What did Trump say about Canada?
The president sounded a similarly optimistic note regarding the US trade war with Canada.
He said Canada was keen to make a deal and that one could be struck "fairly soon," while reiterating his claims that Canada had treated US farmers unfairly with its tariffs.
"Canada ‌wants to make a ‌deal ​very badly," he said.
"Canada has ​to treat our farmers better. ​They can't ‌charge our farmers tariffs," he said, ​adding: "You'll ⁠probably see a deal with Canada ⁠fairly ​soon."

articles.title: Uganda lays 'boy king' Oyo to rest amid succession row
articles.summary: A funeral is underway for King Oyo Nyimba, who was crowned in the Tooro Kingdom in 1995 aged just 3. His death at 34 has triggered a dispute over a successor, as rumors abound of possible heirs born…

image.caption: The funeral has been taking place of King Oyo Nyimba, seen here aged 18 in 2010Image: Marc Hofer/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Uganda has concluded a nine-day period of mourning for King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, with a funeral for the Tooro Kingdom's late monarch due to take place in the western city of Fort Portal on Saturday.

Oyo, who once held the unofficial title of the world's youngest king, ascended the throne as a young child in 1995 and died last month of cancer aged just 34, with his death prompting a bitter succession dispute.

blocks.caption: Oyo's coffin lay in state at the Karuziika Royal PalaceImage: Michael Muhati/REUTERS

blocks.text: How is Oyo to be laid to rest?

The casket carrying the king's body, which was draped in the blue-and-yellow Tooro flag, was carried by hearse from the royal palace in Fort Portal in a procession accompanied by royal guards dressed in orange tunics and beating wooden sticks.
The ceremony in St. John's Cathedral was to be attended by hundreds of mourners, including senior Ugandan government officials.
After the service in the cathedral, Oyo was to be buried at the site of the royal tombs.
At the burial ceremony, tradition dictates that the successor should throw nine coffee berries into the grave.

blocks.caption: Oyo's death has caused widespread griefImage: Abubaker Lubowa/REUTERS

blocks.text: Dispute over Oyo's successor
However, the question of that successor has aroused considerable controversy, and it was in doubt until late on Friday who would carry out that rite.
On Wednesday, a committee made up of members of the royal clan announced it had chosen Oyo's cousin, Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, as the new king.
Kijanangoma, 54, is a news anchor and editor at state broadcaster UBC.
But the immediate family of the late king said that the latter's will had called for a son who was born out of wedlock and has yet to be identified to succeed him.
Additionally, there have been claims on social media that there are at least two possible heirs alleged to be Oyo's children.
Those supporting Kijanangoma say Oyo's family has so far failed to come up with concrete information on the alleged son, while traditionalists also favor the choice of an adult as new monarch.
A source with knowledge ⁠of ​crisis talks on the matter said authorities had managed to get Kijanangoma officially accepted as successor on Friday.

blocks.caption: Mourners queued before the royal palace to view the king's bodyImage: Abubaker Lubowa/REUTERS

blocks.text: Beloved traditional monarchs
Queen Mother Best Kemigisa said in a statement that the succession battle undermined the family's ability to mourn the king's death.
"I also appeal to those fighting over the throne: Please, there will be time for all of that," she said. "Let us grieve and bury my son King Oyo."

Although Uganda is led by an elected head of state, it still possesses several kingdoms that were restored in 1993 after being banned for some three decades following the country's independence from British colonial rule.
The monarchs of such kingdoms are often beloved but hold no formal power. Instead they are seen as guardians of traditional identity and heritage.

articles.title: BRICS summit leaders urge 'maximum restraint' in Middle East
articles.summary: The joint delcaration at the BRICS 2026 summit expressed 'deep concern' over escalation of tensions in the Middle East. China's President Xi.Jingping said the Iran war was not in the bloc's interest.…
articles.byline: Karl Sexton, Felix Tamsut, Midhat Fatimah

image.caption: Xi Jinping is expected to meet Narendra Modi at 5.45 p.m. local timeImage: Mukhtar Khan/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: September 12, 2026
What does the joint declaration say?
On the first day of the BRICS Summit, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the adoption of a joint declaration.
The joint declaration adopted by the BRICS coalition stresses on the need to cooperate to maintain the smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy.

"We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in Middle East/West Asia and, recalling our respective national positions, call for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation," the statement read.
The member states have reiterated their commitment to peaceful resolution of international disputes through dialogue, consultation and diplomacy.
The declaration also advocates for a multilateral approach that respects diverse national viewpoints and positions on crucial global issues.
The bloc expressed its concern about the growing risks of nuclear danger and conflict.

articles.title: Russian GRU spies behind failed Leipzig attack: reports
articles.summary: A German newspaper has cited reports tying a failed attack at Leipzig Airport to Moscow's GRU military intelligence agency. One suspect's ties to GRU were known when he entered the country, yet he…

image.caption: Bomb experts were able to disarm an explosives-laden drone at Leipzig/Halle Airport in a failed attack now definitively attributed to Russia's GRU military intelligence agencyImage: Axel Schmidt/REUTERS

blocks.text: Germany's Welt am Sonntag (WaS) newspaper has cited intelligence reports tying the recent failed drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport directly to Moscow's GRU military intelligence agency.
In an article published on Saturday, Welt am Sonntag said that a man with known ties to the GRU was responsible for operational logistics in the attempted attack.
Further, it said those ties were known to German authorities when the man entered the country from Turkey, nevertheless, he was not surveilled after arrival.
Classified security assessments cited by the paper say the Russian national is now in his home country after departing to Serbia on a flight from Berlin-Brandenburg Airport.
A second man, a Belarus citizen, was also cited as an accomplice in the report.
Germany blames Russia for attempted terror attack in Leipzig
Explosives thought to have entered Germany from Bulgaria and Serbia

German intelligence sources said that the explosives used in the incident were likely smuggled into Germany via truck from Bulgaria and Serbia and then stored in underground depots once they arrived in Leipzig.

Berlin quickly made clear that forensic evidence found at Leipzig/Halle Airport — including drone configuration, explosives and trigger mechanisms used in other Russian hybrid attacks — pointed to a Russian plot.

In early August, German tabloid BILD reported that authorities had found DNA traces on the drone's remote control antenna. Those samples were said to have matched DNA found at the scene of a July 20, 2024, arson attack at a Leipzig logistics facility operated by German courier company DHL.
Leipzig attack averted but Russian escalation will continue

The incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport — a hub for military aid destined for Ukraine — occurred on the evening of August 4 and involved an explosives-laden drone that was found near a Ukrainian transport jet.
Authorities were able to disarm the drone and after public speculation that Moscow was behind the incident the German government officially blamed Russia in early September.
Saturday's article said Berlin made the attribution on the basis of the intelligence reports cited.
In response to its conclusion, Germany announced the closure of the Russian Consulate General in Bonn.
The Kremlin in turn reacted by closing Goethe Institutes — a German cultural exchange outfit — across Russia.
As in numerous similar hybrid attacks prior, Russia has denied any involvement in the incident.
Putin denies Russian involvement in Leipzig drone attack

articles.title: NBI uncovers POC reimbursement, delayed payment for 2019 SEA Games cauldron
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has uncovered additional details in its investigation into the controversial 2019 Southeast Asian Games (SEA Games) cauldron, including what it described as…

blocks.text: Published September 12, 2026 7:25pm

The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has uncovered additional details in its investigation into the controversial 2019 Southeast Asian Games (SEA Games) cauldron, including what it described as a questionable reimbursement involving the Philippine Olympic Committee (POC) and the Philippine Southeast Asian Games Organizing Committee (PHISGOC).

In an exclusive interview in Pasay City, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said investigators found that, aside from the alleged double payment, PHISGOC also received reimbursement from the POC. Matibag said the transaction is now being questioned because the money paid by the POC came from public funds, while PHISGOC is a non-government organization (NGO).
Matibag also said the payment for the cauldron appeared to have been made only as an “afterthought,” noting that it was reportedly settled years after the Philippines hosted the 2019 SEA Games.
The NBI further discovered that the component of the cauldron responsible for producing the flame was rented rather than purchased.
While the cauldron has long been reported to have cost P55 million, Matibag said documents obtained by the NBI show that less than P50 million was actually paid for it.

Following the testimony of a witness who surfaced on Monday, the NBI said it will issue subpoenas to additional personalities as investigators continue to look into the newly disclosed details surrounding the cauldron’s procurement and payment.
The NBI is investigating the alleged anomalous procurement of projects related to the 2019 SEA Games after receiving new information and documents involving PHISGOC. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Elk involved in nearly two-thirds of aggressive encounters in national parks, study finds
articles.summary: Researchers analyzed Parks Canada data collected from 2010 to 2023 on aggressive wildlife encounters and what people were doing when they occurred. The researchers found that quiet activities like…

image.caption: Elk should be given at least three school bus lengths of space, says Nick de Ruyter of the Biosphere Institute of the Bow Valley. Bear spray can also be used to deter an elk if it charges. (Amir Said/CBC)

blocks.text: Calgary

Researchers analyzed Parks Canada data collected from 2010 to 2023 on aggressive wildlife encounters and what people were doing when they occurred. The researchers found that quiet activities like hiking, walking and sightseeing were when many encounters occurred.
Study looked at over 10 years of Parks Canada data on aggressive wildlife encounters
Elk were involved in nearly two-thirds of aggressive wildlife encounters, according to a new study of 25 Canadian national parks.

Researchers analyzed Parks Canada data collected from 2010 to 2023 on aggressive wildlife encounters and what people were doing when they occurred. The study found confrontations happened most often when people were doing quiet, everyday activities like hiking, wildlife watching, sightseeing and strolling in town.
Five animals were examined in the study: elk, mule deer, coyotes, grizzlies and black bears.

Elk were involved with more than 60 per cent of the nearly 3,000 aggressive encounters. They were involved in more than half of the encounters during adventure sports like mountain biking and 80 per cent of encounters at campsites. Elk were also involved in more encounters in town than any other animal.
Study author Shashank Balakrishna says the findings show people don't always recognize which animals can be dangerous.
“Elk are herbivores, and so people tend to believe they aren't as aggressive as a grizzly bear. The results show people are underestimating the power of large herbivores,” he says.
Nick de Ruyter, program director at the Biosphere Institute of the Bow Valley, says the findings don’t surprise him.
Elk spend a lot of time in and around the Town of Banff, he says — in part to stay away from predators.
And because they're used to being around people, de Ruyter says, people can start to see them as tame.
“People get too close. They try to feed them. They try to take photos with them — selfies. And that leads to attacks,” he says.
Eighty per cent of the encounters happened in Banff and Jasper, likely in part because millions of tourists visit the parks every year and there are towns within these two parks, says de Ruyter.
The data groups several types of interactions under “aggressive encounters,” including aggressive displays like stomping, bluff charges and animals chasing people.
Actual attacks made up only 1.6 per cent of encounters.
“The wildlife are actually quite tolerant of people,” de Ruyter says.
Many encounters, such as bluff charges, are actually defensive measures that can signal people are too close.
“So a lot of it comes down to the choices we make. But there should be healthy fear and respect of the wildlife here, because things can go wrong,” he says.
Bears accounted for 27 per cent of aggressive encounters.

Grizzly bear encounters were most commonly associated with low-impact activities, including hiking and walking. De Ruyter says when people are quiet on hiking trails, that leads to more surprise encounters with wildlife.

items: Woman fined after grizzly bear run-in with off-leash dog in Banff National Park
Black bear killed after getting into garbage near Calgary

blocks.text: “Making noise is key,” he says, especially in areas where people can’t see far ahead. Turning a corner quietly, for example, can mean unexpectedly coming across a bear.
Coyotes and mule deer had the least amount of encounters, but when they did become aggressive it was often in town.

items: Bears, caribou and other animals are messing with this researcher's equipment, and he's got photos to prove it

blocks.text: De Ruyter says hiking and walking are among the most common activities in the parks, which could be part of the reason why so many encounters happen during these activities.
Balakrishna agrees his study’s results do not mean hiking is more dangerous. He says they don’t have the data on how many people were doing each activity, so they can’t compare risk.
De Ruyter says people should give animals three school bus lengths of space and carry bear spray, even when walking through busy areas of town.
“People shouldn't be scared. They shouldn't be afraid to go out in the mountains, but they should make good choices and be properly prepared,” he says.

Michelle McCann is a reporter with CBC Bow Valley. You can reach her at michelle.mccann@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Xi Jinping gets red carpet at Brics summit amid thaw in India-China relations
articles.summary:
Chinese president’s arrival in Delhi seen as step towards reconciliation after deadly 2020 military clash

The Chinese president, Xi Jinping, has received a red-carpet welcome in India for a…

blocks.text: The Chinese president, Xi Jinping, has received a red-carpet welcome in India for a summit of Brics developing nations, as regional rivals Beijing and Delhi make a public display of thawing relations while quietly competing to lead at a time of shaky US global dominance.
As Xi stepped off the plane, he was walked past an honour guard of Indian soldiers and traditional dancers in colourful dresses.

The Russian president, Vladimir Putin, and Iranian president, Masoud Pezeshkian, had already been welcomed by the Indian prime minister, Narendra Modi, who is hosting one of the group’s most closely watched gatherings since its inception.

The summit marks Xi’s first visit to India in seven years and is seen as the biggest step towards reconciliation after a deadly 2020 military clash along the disputed Himalayan border, in which ‌20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers were killed.

Ties between the nuclear-armed Asian giants have been warming recently, with flights and high-level contacts gradually being restored. China was “willing” to work with India to properly manage differences and be “good neighbours and friends”, China’s foreign ministry said on Friday.

Leaders and diplomats have been convening in India for the annual gathering of the Brics grouping, named after five of its earliest members – Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa – that was conceived as a counterweight to western dominance.
This summit comes as wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, along with rising US-China tensions, test the bloc’s ability to find common ground.

Since its inception in 2009, Brics has expanded as a forum for major emerging economies to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The group now rivals the US-dominated G7 forum of advanced economies, accounting for half of the global population.

But its growth has also created new fractures and disunity – Iran was bombing Saudi Arabia and the UAE earlier this year, and Brics foreign ministers failed to agree on a joint statement when they met in Delhi in May.
Reuters reported on Saturday that India’s summit would result in a generic joint declaration that would show unity by condemning unilateral war, but ⁠was unlikely to ​name any single country.
Jiang Shixue, vice-president of the expert committee of the China thinktank Council for BRICs cooperation (China), said the 11 members “cannot speak with one voice on many issues”.
“The only solution is to continuously strengthen political consensus,” he told the South China Morning Post.
Beijing and Delhi have differing views on the role of the group.

China has sought to expand Brics power as a counterweight to the US under Donald Trump’s leadership, which has launched global tariff and trade wars and retreated from multilateral institutions such as the UN, which afforded it international credibility.
India has taken a more cautious approach, seeing Brics as a bridge between the west and the developing world.

Chietigj Bajpaee, a senior research fellow for South Asia in the Asia-Pacific programme at Chatham House, said this week that Delhi had found it hard to maintain its policy of “strategic hedging” during such a disruptive US presidency.

“India’s position can appear out of sync in a forum whose membership includes countries with more overtly anti-western agendas, including China, Russia and Iran. And two other Brics countries, South Africa and Brazil, have suffered high-profile diplomatic disputes with the US,” he wrote.
“The challenge for Delhi is that it wishes to promote this worldview in a way that is non-western but not explicitly anti-western.”
Agence France-Presse contributed to this report

articles.title: Comelec removes with finality Moro Ako Party from BARMM 2026 poll roster
articles.summary: The Commission on Elections (Comelec) has ruled with finality on the disqualification of the Moro Ako Party from the Major Regional Parliamentary Political Party (RPPP) roster for the upcoming BARMM…

blocks.text: Published September 12, 2026 6:31pm

The Commission on Elections (Comelec) has ruled with finality on the disqualification of the Moro Ako Party from the Major Regional Parliamentary Political Party (RPPP) roster for the upcoming BARMM parliamentary elections.

In a Certificate of Finality and Entry of Judgment dated September 7, 2026, the Commission said it did not receive a motion for reconsideration on the en banc ruling that affirmed Moro Ako's disqualification.

The motion could have been filed within five days of the party's receipt of the August 27 resolution of the Commission en Banc, with the intent to preclude the order from being final and executory, according to the document which was made public on Saturday.
In the August 27 ruling, the Commission En Banc affirmed its decision to deny the appeal of Moro Ako Party for "lack of merit."

The poll body dismissed Moro Ako's appeal regarding the cancellation of its registration and accreditation as an RPPP after the party failed to satisfy registration requirements and allegedly committed material misrepresentation.
Under Comelec Resolution 11271, the cancellation of Moro Ako Party's registration and accreditation is considered final and executory.

"Its accreditation as a Major RPPP is deemed revoked, and all entitlements, privileges, and preferences granted to it, including the allotment of the 12th copy of the election returns and the privilege to appoint watchers, are hereby withdrawn," it added.
